name: Suet Paste
description: Historical recipe from Miss Leslie's Complete Cookery (1851). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

instructions.text: Remove the skin and stringy fibres from a pound of beef suet, and chop it as fine as possible.
Sift two quarts of flour into a deep pan, and rub into it one half of the suet.
Make it into a round lump of dough with cold water, and then knead it a little.
Lay the dough on your paste-board, roll it out very thin, and cover it with the remaining half of the suet.
Flour it, roll it out thin again, and then roll it into a scroll.
Cut it into as many pieces as you want sheets of paste, and roll them out half an inch thick.

source.author: Eliza Leslie
source.originalInstructions:
1. Remove the skin and stringy fibres from a pound of beef suet, and chop it as fine as possible.
2. Sift two quarts of flour into a deep pan, and rub into it one half of the suet.
3. Make it into a round lump of dough with cold water, and then knead it a little.
4. Lay the dough on your paste-board, roll it out very thin, and cover it with the remaining half of the suet.
5. Flour it, roll it out thin again, and then roll it into a scroll.
6. Cut it into as many pieces as you want sheets of paste, and roll them out half an inch thick.
